brief.summary_1line: Vishwamitra narrates the churning of the ocean, Shiva drinking poison, Vishnu supporting Mandara as Kurma, and the devas’ eventual victory for the nectar.

image_candidates.scene_text: The gods and demons pull the serpent Vasuki around Mount Mandara as it churns the ocean of milk, with foam and waves rising around them.
Lord Shiva calmly drinks the deadly cosmic poison while the terrified gods watch and plead for salvation.
Vishnu as a gigantic tortoise supports Mount Mandara on his back beneath the ocean while devas and asuras continue the churning above.

deep.rich_summary: As Rama and Lakshmana travel with the sage Vishwamitra, they reach the beautiful city of Vishala. At Rama’s request, Vishwamitra recounts a cosmic legend he once heard from Indra: the churning of the Ocean of Milk. Devas and asuras, seeking immortality, use Mount Mandara as a churning rod and the serpent Vasuki as a rope. The process releases a catastrophic poison that threatens the universe until Shiva compassionately drinks it. Vishnu then supports the sinking mountain in the form of a tortoise. From the ocean emerge wonders—Dhanvantari, countless apsaras, Varuni, the celestial horse Uchchaishravas, the Kaustubha jewel, and finally the nectar of immortality—triggering a fierce battle in which Vishnu, as the enchantress Mohini, secures victory for the gods.

highlight_spans.why: A sacred framing that promises spiritual merit to anyone who hears or recites the story, emphasizing the myth’s religious importance.
The pivotal setup of the cosmic churning: devas and asuras using Mount Mandara and the serpent Vasuki to churn the Ocean of Milk.
Shiva’s dramatic act of compassion—drinking the deadly poison to save gods and the world.
Vishnu’s Kurma (tortoise) incarnation supporting the mountain, a central mythological revelation in Hindu cosmology.
The climax: Vishnu’s enchanting Mohini form deceives the combatants and secures the nectar for the gods.

top_scenes.scene_text: Mount Mandara spins in the Ocean of Milk while devas and asuras pull the serpent Vasuki from opposite sides, waves and divine energy erupting around them.
Shiva calmly drinks the deadly cosmic poison as terrified gods look on, the dark venom glowing in his throat against the backdrop of the churning ocean.
Vishnu as the enchanting Mohini stands amid the warring devas and asuras, gracefully holding the pot of nectar while the armies pause in awe and confusion.
